heroHeadline: 48th ASEAN Summit Opens in Cebu: First Charter Amendment Since 2007 ('Cebu Protocol'), ASEAN Maritime Centre for Philippines Proposed — Lazaro Chairs 59th AMM as Balikatan 2026 Enters Final Day
heroSubtitle: The 48th ASEAN Leaders' Summit opened its substantive proceedings on May 7, 2026 in Cebu with the 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting (AMM), chaired by Philippine DFA Secretary Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro. Foreign ministers from all 10 ASEAN member states convened at the Shangri-La Mactan Resort with maritime security and South China Sea Code of Conduct negotiations as centerpiece agenda items, alongside Myanmar's post-coup reintegration question. The Summit is set to adopt the 'Cebu Protocol to Amend the ASEAN Charter' — the first amendment to the ASEAN Charter since it was signed in 2007 — primarily to accommodate Timor-Leste's full membership as ASEAN's 11th state (acceded October 2025). Leaders are also expected to endorse an ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on Maritime Cooperation that would formalize the ASEAN Coast Guard Forum as a permanent sectoral body and establish an ASEAN Maritime Centre in the Philippines (Philstar, Manila Times). The 48th Summit plenary follows on May 8, concurrent with the closing ceremonies for Balikatan 2026 — the largest-ever iteration with 17,000+ troops from 7 nations — which ends the same day after 19 days of exercises including the landmark Japan-US-Australia-Philippines SINKEX off Ilocos Norte (May 6). The Sandy Cay 1 flag-duel sovereignty theater, the Atin Ito civilian coalition's successful landing (May 3), and China's copycat flag placement dismissed as 'planted trash' (May 5-6) frame the geopolitical atmosphere entering the ASEAN plenary. COC finalization in 2026 remains assessed as 'simply not achievable' by analysts and China's own expert Wu Shicun, despite ASEAN reaffirming the 2026 target.
